answer: Agents can require each identity to post a bond that is gradually unlocked only after completing useful work verified by randomly assigned peers. If one operator creates a swarm of fake agents, each must lock up real funds, while the swarm’s coordinated reviews are more likely to expose an echo of shared behavior and trigger bond slashing. A falcon watching for duplicate activity can flag suspicious clusters, but the defense does not depend on perfect detection: sybils tie up capital and risk losing it before reaching the zenith of influence.
